requirement.title: Truthful, Bounded Worktree Timeout Reporting
requirement.body:
Worktree tool timeout responses must not assert a cause they did not test, and must not advise an action that cannot succeed.

The timeout branches of adv_worktree_cleanup, adv_worktree_delete, and adv_worktree_detach resolve a setTimeout sentinel rather than a rejection, so no error object exists to classify. These responses must therefore not assert a poisoned workflow and must not carry an unconditional adv_doctor referral, unless poison evidence was actually collected on that call (see rq-worktreePoisonVisibility01).

Timeout remediation must name an action that can actually succeed. When the caller's timeoutMs was clamped to the safe budget, the response must not advise passing a larger timeoutMs, must state that the safe budget is a structural ceiling, and must not name an option the current mode ignores.

On timeout, adv_worktree_cleanup must report the stage in flight (discovery or drain), captured synchronously before any post-timeout await, plus either pendingDeleteCount or pendingDeleteCountUnavailable when the pending-delete read fails. An empty queue and an unreadable queue must remain distinguishable.

adv_worktree_cleanup accepts an optional skipDiscovery flag (worktrees mode only) providing drain-only recovery of already-queued pending deletes after a prior cleanup timed out during discovery. Drain-only must not delete worktrees that discovery never validated.

Git subprocesses on the cleanup discovery path must each be bounded strictly below the tool budget, derived per-call as min(2000, floor(effectiveTimeoutMs / 4)). Shared git helpers retain their original defaults when invoked from non-cleanup paths.

# Fix adv_worktree_cleanup timeout remediation and diagnosis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Observed.** While cleaning up after archiving `fixArtifactReadFallback`:

- Call 1, no `timeoutMs`: `{"success":false,"timedOut":true,"effectiveTimeoutMs":8000,"error":"adv_worktree_cleanup timed out after 8000ms. Cleanup likely blocked on a poisoned workflow or stuck I/O. Retry after the underlying workflow is resolved (see adv_doctor).","remediation":"Pass a larger timeoutMs (clamped to the safe budget) to retry, or run adv_doctor to classify and repair the poisoned workflow first."}`
- Call 2, `timeoutMs: 30000`: `"adv_worktree_cleanup timed out after 8000ms (requested 30000ms was clamped to safe budget 8000ms)."` — accompanied by the identical remediation telling the caller to pass a larger `timeoutMs`.

The worktree was clean, its branch fully merged to `origin/trunk`, and a manual `git worktree remove` completed instantly. Nothing was stuck.

**The clamp is correct and must not change.** `WORKTREE_TOOL_SAFE_TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000` (`plugin/src/tools/adv-worktree.ts:52`) is a deliberate, spec-anchored invariant under `rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup02` (`.adv/specs/worktree-lifecycle/spec.json:559-583`). It sits below the SDK's 10s `DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS` so the tool's own `Promise.race` resolves first and returns a typed, actionable response instead of an opaque `ToolExecutionTimeout`. `clampToSafeBudget` (`plugin/src/tools/adv-worktree.ts:69-81`) is monotone downward — no input raises the effective budget.

### Defect 1 — remediation advises a structurally impossible action

The `remediation` string at `plugin/src/tools/adv-worktree.ts:381-382` is emitted unconditionally. The adjacent `error` text IS conditional on the clamp via `clampedNote` (lines 372-374), but the remediation is a fixed literal. So a caller who has just been told their `30000` was clamped to `8000` is advised, in the next field, to pass a larger `timeoutMs`. Following the advice can never succeed. The `archived_branches` mode carries the same defect at lines 316-317.

### Defect 2 — the poison diagnosis is asserted without evidence

`"Cleanup likely blocked on a poisoned workflow or stuck I/O"` (`plugin/src/tools/adv-worktree.ts:380`) is a hardcoded literal inside the timeout branch, fired the moment `_timedOut` is detected at line 371. No poison detection runs anywhere on the cleanup path: neither `advWorktreeCleanup` (`plugin/src/tools/worktree/index.ts:3161-3192`), nor `discoverTerminalCleanupCandidates` (lines 2911-2978), nor `drainPendingDeletes` (lines 3020-3153) calls `describeWorkflowExecution` or inspects an error class. The real poison-detection path (`plugin/src/tools/worktree/state.ts:975-1116`) is never invoked. This contradicts `rq-worktreePoisonVisibility01` (`.adv/specs/worktree-lifecycle/spec.json:46-94`), which requires error class plus structured warnings before classifying poison. The tool points the caller at `adv_doctor` on the strength of a guess it never tested — and in this instance the guess was wrong.

### Contributing factor — sequential discovery is what consumes the budget

`discoverTerminalCleanupCandidates` iterates worktrees sequentially (`plugin/src/tools/worktree/index.ts:2930-2975`). Per worktree it runs `git status --porcelain`, a Temporal `store.changes.get` bounded at 1500ms (`DEFAULT_CHANGE_STATUS_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`, line 141), and for non-terminal changes a `gh pr list` shell-out bounded at 1500ms (line 1811). With the 8 worktrees present, two or three slow Temporal or network reads exhaust the 8s budget before the drain phase begins. Because `withTimeout` is explicitly non-cancelling (`plugin/src/utils/with-timeout.ts:30-31`), a retry re-does the same work against the same budget and fails identically — which matches the two observed calls.

### No recovery path exists

`drainPendingDeletes` records `TIMEOUT` failures and retains the queue entries (lines 3131-3148), so a retry inherits the same expensive discovery phase and the same 8s ceiling. There is no `skipDiscovery` or drain-only mode. Manual `git worktree remove` is the de facto recovery, which is what was used here.

## Proposed direction

1. Make `remediation` conditional on `wasClamped` in both the worktrees and `archived_branches` timeout branches, so a clamped caller is told the 8s budget is a structural ceiling and given an action that can actually succeed.
2. Stop asserting poison without evidence — either drop the claim or attach the real inner error. Keep the honest signal that the cause is unknown.
3. Consider bounded-concurrency discovery (the `INVENTORY_INTERNAL_BUDGET_MS` infrastructure already imported at `plugin/src/tools/adv-worktree.ts:12` is used this way by `adv_worktree_triage`), and optionally a drain-only mode so a timed-out cleanup has a structural recovery rather than a manual one.

**Explicitly out of scope:** raising `WORKTREE_TOOL_SAFE_TIMEOUT_MS`. Doing so would violate `rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup02` and forfeit the typed-response guarantee.

## Why it matters

Low severity but high friction. The tool's guidance is self-contradictory, and the unfounded poison claim routes operators to `adv_doctor` for a condition that does not exist — the same class of misdirection tracked separately for Temporal read errors.

# Agreement — Fix cleanup timeout remediation and diagnosis

## Objectives

1. Never advise an impossible action. A caller whose `timeoutMs` was clamped must not be told to pass a larger `timeoutMs`.
2. Never assert a diagnosis the code did not test. The timeout response must not claim a poisoned workflow when no poison detection ran.
3. Give the operator a recovery path that is not `git worktree remove` by hand.
4. Close the bounded-I/O gap that makes the 8s budget exhaust in the first place.

## Discovery findings that shape this agreement

| # | Finding | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Timeout branch races a `setTimeout` sentinel, not a rejection — there is no error object | Objective 2 is satisfied by removing the claim, not by reclassifying. `classifyWorktreeWorkflowFailure` has nothing to consume here. |
| D2 | `discover?: boolean` already exists on `AdvWorktreeCleanupDeps` (`worktree/index.ts:2878`); startup drain already uses it. The tool wrapper (`adv-worktree.ts:350-358`) never forwards it | Drain-only recovery is a forwarding gap, not new machinery. |
| D3 | Git subprocesses on the discovery path are bounded, but bounded ABOVE the tool budget. The local `git()` in `worktree/index.ts:850` uses `timeout: 30000`; the local `git()` in `census.ts:24` uses `timeout: 10_000`. Only `utils/git.ts:19` `execGit` (5000ms default) sits below the 8s ceiling | Violates the `rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup02` body: internal operations must each be bounded below the tool budget. A single slow `git rev-parse` can consume 30s inside an  8s ceiling. This is the real budget-exhaustion cause. Corrected from an initial reconnaissance claim of "unbounded", which direct source reading disproved. |
| D4 | Triage already returns typed partial results — `complete` / `stopReason` / `stoppedStage` / `omitted` (`triage.ts:261-282`, `adv-worktree.ts:931-949`) | Proven in-repo shape to reuse for a partial cleanup timeout response. |
| D5 | `rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup01` mandates sequential per-item cleanup. Discovery writes pending-delete records via `setPendingDelete` | Bounded-concurrency discovery carries spec-adjacent risk. Deferred. |

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Given `adv_worktree_cleanup` is called with a `timeoutMs` above the safe budget and the call times out in either `worktrees` or `archived_branches` mode, when the typed timeout response is produced, then the `remediation` field does not instruct the caller to pass a larger `timeoutMs` and instead states that the safe budget is a structural ceiling and names an action that can actually succeed.
- AC2: Given `adv_worktree_cleanup` times out with no clamp applied because the caller requested no timeout or one at or below the safe budget, when the typed timeout response is produced, then the `remediation` field may still offer a larger `timeoutMs` because that action is reachable.
- AC3: Given `adv_worktree_cleanup` times out without collecting any poison evidence on that call, when the `error` string is produced, then it contains no assertion that a workflow is poisoned and no unconditional referral to `adv_doctor`.
- AC4: Given `adv_worktree_cleanup` times out, when the typed timeout response is produced, then it reports which stage was in flight as discovery or drain and reports any progress counters already accumulated, following the existing triage partial-result shape.
- AC5: Given a prior cleanup timed out during discovery and left pending-delete entries queued, when the caller invokes `adv_worktree_cleanup` requesting drain-only, then discovery is skipped and the queued pending deletes are drained within the same safe budget.
- AC6: Given any git subprocess invoked on the cleanup discovery path, when that subprocess hangs, then it is terminated by its own timeout strictly below the tool budget and discovery either continues or self-returns a partial result rather than relying on the outer race as its only guard.
- AC7: `WORKTREE_TOOL_SAFE_TIMEOUT_MS` remains 8000, `clampToSafeBudget` remains monotone downward, `effectiveTimeoutMs` remains reported in every response, and the existing `rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup02` acceptance criteria .1 through .5 remain green.

## Constraints

- C1: `rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup02` — clamp value, typed timeout response, no late background mutation, `effectiveTimeoutMs` reporting.
- C2: `rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup01` — per-item cleanup sequential, max 5 retries, no unbounded parallel deletion.
- C3: `rq-terminalCleanupSafety01` — deletion authority stays with `advWorktreeDelete`; no direct `git worktree remove`.
- C4: `rq-worktreePoisonVisibility01` — poison classification requires error-class plus structured evidence; never a guess.
- C5: Drain-only mode must not become a way to delete worktrees that discovery never validated; it drains only entries a prior discovery already queued.
- C6: Tightening git timeouts on the cleanup discovery path must not change the timeout behaviour of the same shared helpers when called from non-cleanup paths such as delete, triage, and archive.

## Avoidances

- DONT1: Raising `WORKTREE_TOOL_SAFE_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- DONT2: Attaching a late-success handler to a timed-out promise, explicitly forbidden by `rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup02.3`.
- DONT3: Adding a `handle.describe()` probe to the timeout branch, since it is itself a Temporal round trip that can hang 10s on a poisoned workflow.
- DONT4: Parallelizing deletion.
- DONT5: Reporting progress counters that were mutated after the timeout response was already produced.

## Out of scope

- OOS1: Bounded-concurrency discovery via `mapWithConcurrency`. Deferred, not rejected. It works mechanically, but discovery writes pending-delete state and `rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup01` draws its sequential line around cleanup processing. Bounding the git I/O attacks the same latency with no spec-boundary argument. Revisit as a follow-up with a spec amendment discussion if AC6 proves insufficient.
- OOS2: Changing the poison-detection machinery itself in `state.ts` or `recovery-probe.ts`.

# Design — Fix cleanup timeout remediation and diagnosis

Four workstreams mapped to acceptance criteria. WS1–WS3 are localised to `adv-worktree.ts` + a thin forwarding seam. WS4 is the most invasive and touches shared git helpers under a C6-preserving default.

**Post-validation revision.** Independent validator (adv-researcher, report `fixCleanupTimeoutRemediation|change:researcher:design-validation|adv-researcher|1`) returned CONDITIONAL. Conditions incorporated: WS1 mode-aware remediation (was recreating AC1 in `archived_branches`), WS2 pending-delete count via existing reader (no new helper), WS4 C6-flow + scope clarifications, WS5 regression tests. Verdict: no redesign required.

## WS1 — Truthful remediation text (AC1, AC2, AC3)

**Files:** `plugin/src/tools/adv-worktree.ts` only.

Two timeout branches carry the defect:

| Mode | Lines | Current defect |
|---|---|---|
| `archived_branches` | 306–320 | unconditional remediation telling caller to pass larger `timeoutMs` |
| `worktrees` | 371–386 | same + hardcoded "likely blocked on a poisoned workflow" |

**Change.** Make `remediation` conditional on `wasClamped`, mirroring the existing `clampedNote` pattern on `error`. Drop the poison assertion from both `error` strings. **Mode-aware clamped-case remediation** — `skipDiscovery` is only honored in `worktrees` mode; `archived_branches` routes to `cleanupArchivedMergedBranches` (line 277) and never forwards `discover`. Naming `skipDiscovery` in the archived_branches clamped case would recreate the AC1 defect class.

For `worktrees` mode (line 371+):
```
remediation = wasClamped
  ? "The ${WORKTREE_TOOL_SAFE_TIMEOUT_MS}ms safe budget is a structural ceiling (rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup02) and cannot be raised. Retry with skipDiscovery:true to drain already-queued deletes, or run adv_worktree_triage to inspect retained candidates."
  : "Retry with a larger timeoutMs (clamped to the safe budget), or run adv_worktree_triage to inspect retained candidates.";
```

For `archived_branches` mode (line 306+) — `skipDiscovery` invalid, name reachable actions only:
```
remediation = wasClamped
  ? "The ${WORKTREE_TOOL_SAFE_TIMEOUT_MS}ms safe budget is a structural ceiling (rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup02) and cannot be raised. Re-run with a narrower changeId filter, or run adv_worktree_triage to inspect merged archived branches individually."
  : "Retry with a larger timeoutMs (clamped to the safe budget), or investigate a stuck git process / unreachable store.";
```

`error` in both modes drops the poison clause. `worktrees` mode becomes (stage from WS2): `"adv_worktree_cleanup timed out after ${effectiveTimeoutMs}ms${clampedNote} during ${stage}. The inner promise was not cancelled; queued deletes may still resolve on a later drain pass."` The `during ${stage}` segment requires WS2 and is omitted from `archived_branches` error text (that mode has no stage tracking).

## WS2 — Stage reporting (AC4)

**Files:** `plugin/src/tools/adv-worktree.ts`, `plugin/src/tools/worktree/index.ts`, `plugin/src/tools/worktree/state.ts` (read-only use of existing reader).

**Why callback, not split race or return-handle.** `advWorktreeCleanup` (`worktree/index.ts:3161-3192`) is a single async function with discovery→drain phases. Splitting it into two separately-raced promises would break its current shape and force every caller to change. A return-handle `{ promise, getStage }` is rejected because `status.ts:875` calls `advWorktreeCleanup` with no stage tracking and would be forced to change; the optional callback leaves it untouched. Callback mirrors how `triage.ts:244-251` tracks `stoppedStage` via local mutation read synchronously at `buildResult` (277).

**Change.**

1. Add to `AdvWorktreeCleanupDeps` (`worktree/index.ts:2878`):
   ```
   onStageEnter?: (stage: "discovery" | "drain") => void;
   ```
2. `advWorktreeCleanup` calls `deps.onStageEnter?.("discovery")` before line 3175 and `deps.onStageEnter?.("drain")` before line 3186.
3. Tool wrapper (`adv-worktree.ts:350-358`) creates `let currentStage: "discovery" | "drain" | "pre" = "pre"` and passes `onStageEnter: (s) => { currentStage = s; }`.
4. Timeout branch reads `currentStage` synchronously. Single-threaded JS guarantees the inner promise's microtasks cannot mutate it between the timeout firing and the response being returned.

**Progress counters (AC4, respecting DONT5).** Do NOT read `removed`/`retained` from the still-running inner promise — those locals are at risk of late mutation and there is no synchronous snapshot seam. Use the existing `getPendingDeletes(database)` reader (`state.ts:479`); inline `(await getPendingDeletes(database)).length` at timeout time. **No new helper** — the validator confirmed `getPendingDeleteCount` does not exist and the existing reader suffices.

```
const pendingDeleteCount = (await getPendingDeletes(database).catch(() => [])).length;
```

This is the count of entries discovery queued (or that a prior run queued) but drain did not yet clear — the actionable number for the operator. Minor staleness (drain may mutate the queue during the async read) is inherent to any snapshot and not a DONT5 violation because we are not attaching a late-success handler. Response shape gains:

```
stage: currentStage,
pendingDeleteCount: <number>,
```

`archived_branches` mode already self-returns `partial` / `omissions`; it does not use stage tracking (routes to `cleanupArchivedMergedBranches`, never calls `advWorktreeCleanup`). AC4 is `worktrees`-mode-scoped.

## WS3 — Drain-only recovery (AC5)

**Files:** `plugin/src/tools/adv-worktree.ts` only.

**C5 satisfaction.** Drain-only is not a new deletion path. `drainPendingDeletes` (`worktree/index.ts:3020-3153`) processes only entries already in the pending-delete table — entries that a prior discovery call validated and queued via `setPendingDelete`. `skipDiscovery:true` cannot delete worktrees discovery never approved.

**Change.**

1. Add `skipDiscovery?: boolean` to `WorktreeCleanupArgs` (`adv-worktree.ts:132-138`).
2. Add to the inline Zod schema (`adv-worktree.ts:804-833`):
   ```
   skipDiscovery: z.boolean().optional().describe(
     "Skip the discovery scan and drain only already-queued pending deletes. Only honored in mode=worktrees (the default); ignored in mode=archived_branches. Use after a prior cleanup timed out during discovery and left entries queued."
   ),
   ```
3. Forward in the tool wrapper (`adv-worktree.ts:350-358`):
   ```
   ...(args.skipDiscovery !== undefined && { discover: !args.skipDiscovery }),
   ```
   Merging `discover: true` from caller is harmless because `advWorktreeCleanup` already defaults to `discover !== false`.

**Mode interaction.** `skipDiscovery` + `mode:archived_branches` is a documented no-op (schema description states it). The archived-branches path never reads `args.skipDiscovery`. Zod rejection was considered and rejected — a no-op preserves callers that set the flag defensively across mode switches.

## WS4 — Bounded discovery git I/O (AC6)

**Files:** `plugin/src/tools/worktree/index.ts`, `plugin/src/tools/worktree/census.ts`, `plugin/src/tools/adv-worktree.ts`.

**Approach: thread a single `gitTimeoutMs` through the cleanup discovery path.** Not an `InventoryBudget`-style deadline — that would be a bigger refactor and the WS2 stage reporting already makes aggregate overruns visible. A per-call timeout below the tool budget satisfies AC6's wording ("strictly below the tool budget") and is mechanically minimal.

**C6 satisfaction — explicit flows.** Every changed helper gains an optional `gitTimeoutMs?: number` parameter that **defaults to its current value**. Non-cleanup callers pass no value and see no change. Two flows to state explicitly:

1. **Cleanup-internal delete:** `gitTimeoutMs` on `AdvWorktreeDeleteDeps` flows into `drainPendingDeletes:3096-3107` which spreads `deps` into `advWorktreeDelete`. So cleanup-triggered deletes also get the tightened timeout. This is safe: failure mode is retention (`recordPendingDeleteFailure`), and the inner `operationTimeoutMs` (`3104`) already bounds the delete operation separately.
2. **Standalone `adv_worktree_delete`:** constructs its own `AdvWorktreeDeleteDeps` (`adv-worktree.ts:224-248`) without `gitTimeoutMs` → helpers default to 30000ms → C6 holds.

**Scope — complete call-site audit (validator-confirmed).** Discovery-reachable `git()` calls from `discoverTerminalCleanupCandidates` (`index.ts:2911-2978`):

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `census.ts:72` `for-each-ref` | census `git()` | 10_000 |
| 2 | `census.ts:77` `branch --merged` | census `git()` | 10_000 |
| 3 | `census.ts:78` `worktree list --porcelain` | census `git()` | 10_000 |
| 4 | `census.ts:94` `status --porcelain` (per-worktree, sequential) | census `git()` | 10_000 |
| 5 | `index.ts:1787` `rev-parse` | index `git()` | 30_000 |
| 6 | `index.ts:1872` `fetch origin` (per merged PR) | index `git()` | 30_000 |
| 7 | `index.ts:1877` `merge-base --is-ancestor` (per merged PR) | index `git()` | 30_000 |

**Out of WS4 scope (delete-path only, not discovery-reachable):**
- `getMergedBranchesForDelete:1728` — called only from `verifyNonAdvBranchIntegration:1934`, itself reached only at `2251, 2306` (inside `advWorktreeDelete`).
- `verifyMissingRegistryChangeBranchIntegration:1964-2023` — called only at `2274` (delete path).

**Shared-helper C6 risk — none.** `census.ts` `git()` is private with one production caller (`scanGitWorkspaceFacts`). `index.ts` `git()` is private; only `getPrMergedBranchIntegration` forwards `gitTimeoutMs` from cleanup; other callers (`branchExists`, `getMergedBranchesForDelete`, create/prune paths) don't forward it → default preserved.

```

Normal clean-worktree status ≈ 10–50ms. Scaling (`effectiveTimeoutMs / Math.max(4, worktreeCount)`) was considered and rejected — adds complexity for a pathological case already covered by the outer race.

**Changes.**

1. `worktree/index.ts:850` local `git()` helper — add optional third parameter:
   ```

   ```
2. `census.ts:24` local `git()` helper — add optional third parameter:
   ```
   async function git(cwd, args, timeoutMs = 10_000): Promise<string> { ... timeout: timeoutMs ... }
   ```
3. `scanGitWorkspaceFacts(repoRoot, defaultBranch, gitTimeoutMs?)` — thread `gitTimeoutMs` to all four `git()` calls (lines 72–78 parallel trio + line 94 per-worktree status).
4. `AdvWorktreeDeleteDeps` — add `gitTimeoutMs?: number`. Thread through every `git()` call site inside `getPrMergedBranchIntegration` (lines 1787, 1872, 1877).
5. `AdvWorktreeCleanupDeps` — add `gitTimeoutMs?: number`, forwarded to `AdvWorktreeDeleteDeps` inside `advWorktreeCleanup`.

# Executive Summary

## Outcome

When worktree maintenance commands run out of time, they now tell the operator the truth about what happened and offer a next step that actually works. You are approving a self-contained correctness fix to internal maintenance tooling — no user-facing product surface changes.

## Why It Matters

The tool previously gave contradictory guidance: it would tell an operator their requested time limit had been reduced, then in the very next line advise them to request a longer one — advice that could never succeed. It also blamed a specific internal fault ("poisoned workflow") that it had never actually checked for, sending operators to a repair tool for a problem that did not exist. In the incident that prompted this change, nothing was stuck at all; the operator fell back to deleting the worktree by hand.

Investigation and review each widened the fix in a way that mattered. Investigation found a genuine rule violation: the project's own cleanup standard requires every internal step to finish inside the overall time budget, but two internal steps were allowed to run three to four times longer than the whole operation — the real reason the operation ran out of time. Hardening then found the same false-diagnosis defect still live in two neighbouring commands, which are now fixed too.

## Verdict

APPROVED — release ready

## What Was Built

1. **Truthful guidance when time runs out** — advice is tailored to what actually happened and differs correctly between the tool's two modes, so it never recommends an option that mode does not support.
2. **Honest reporting instead of guessing** — the unfounded fault diagnosis was removed from three commands, not just the one reported. Each now reports what it actually knows.
3. **A real recovery path** — operators can ask the tool to skip the slow scan and finish already-approved queued work, instead of resorting to manual deletion.
4. **Root cause closed** — every internal step now finishes well inside the overall budget, so one slow step can no longer consume the entire allowance.
5. **Distinguishable failure reporting** — an empty work queue and an unreadable one are no longer both reported as zero.
6. **Protection against silent regression** — added the guard proving the original time limits still apply to unrelated callers, which review found missing.
7. **Written standard updated** — the capability spec now describes the shipped behaviour, so future audits can verify it.

## What Was Verified

- Review verdict: APPROVED with 11 findings (0 blockers, 4 issues, 5 suggestions, 2 nits). All 4 issues fixed; 2 findings rejected as incorrect after direct verification; remainder deferred with evidence.
- Hardening: no blockers, no high findings. 2 medium findings — the neighbouring false-diagnosis sites — were fixed rather than deferred, with your approval.
- Tests: 142 passed across the affected areas. Full project checks pass clean.
- Merge compatibility: clean, zero commits behind the mainline.
- Preview URL: not_applicable — no browser-visible or visual output; this changes command-line tool text and internal timeout values.
- Contract matrix: 19 of 19 required items passed or respected. Zero failed, violated, or unknown.

## Remaining Concerns

Non-blocking:

1. **Deployment is a separate step.** This is a plugin change; it will not affect the live tool until built, deployed, and the host restarted. Normal for this repo.
2. **A tighter network timeout could retain more worktrees.** Repository lookups over slow links now have a 2-second limit rather than 30. The failure mode is safe — the worktree is kept, never wrongly deleted — but worth watching after deploy.
3. **Two deferred test-quality suggestions.** Faster tests using simulated clocks, and one decorative assertion. Neither affects correctness.
4. **Four unrelated project tests are failing.** Independently confirmed pre-existing — they fail identically on the untouched mainline at this change's starting point. Logged for separate triage.

## Supporting Evidence

- Tasks: tk-7b2d308848b0, tk-2a69e7c2a549, tk-b4217ae3eb05, tk-6d217e1bba98, tk-57abcd25de71

- Spec delta: rq-worktreeTimeoutTruthfulness01, 7 scenarios
- Design independently validated; review used three scanners, one of whose claims was disproved by direct execution and rejected

## Release Readiness Summary

Release-ready. Hardening ran production, deployment, and documentation readiness checks plus inline cleanup and merge-compatibility verification. No blockers, no high findings. The two medium findings were same-defect siblings in the touched file and were fixed under the campsite rule with your explicit approval, rather than deferred.

Cleanup is clean: no temporary files, no debug code, no skipped or disabled tests introduced. Merge dry-run against the mainline is conflict-free. The one documentation gap found — operators had no written reference for the new recovery option — was closed in the cleanup command contract.
